title: Economic Incentives and Routing Behavior of LLM-Based Driver Agents in Ride-Hailing Markets
authors: Beiming Hu; Paul Chung; Jason Fang
abstract: The integration of large language models (LLMs) into urban mobility systems introduces new opportunities for simulating complex behavioral dynamics, particularly in ride-hailing markets. While these models show theoretical promise as autonomous proxies for human decision-makers, it is still unclear how effectively they navigate within strategic spatial economies. To determine if LLMs can authentically comprehend the values and replicate the routing behavior of human drivers under various economic context, this study evaluates four LLMs (ChatGPT 5.2, Gemini 3.0, DeepSeek V3.2, and Claude Sonnet 4.6). Using a stated-choice empirical framework, we subject these agents to combinations of fare schemes, surge multipliers, and varying passenger occupancies. By analyzing the fundamental trade-off between travel time and trip revenue, we compare the agents&apos; economic sensitivity against historical human taxi driver data. Our findings indicate that, at an aggregate level, LLM agents successfully interpret complex operating conditions and execute time-cost trade-offs comparable to human baselines. However, behavioral fidelity is highly model-dependent; notably, the routing consistency of DeepSeek V3.2 and Gemini 3.0 degrades under intense market incentives and heightened spatial complexity. Overall, our findings suggest that while LLMs demonstrate significant potential as behavioral simulators for transportation policy and planning, the their sensitivity to various economic contexts and cross-model heterogeneity necessitate more than simple performance alignment before deployment. Instead, their application in transportation networks should be supported by rigorous model-specific validation, staged and context-sensitive implementation, and adaptive governance mechanisms designed to ensure behavioral reliability, regulatory compatibility, and resilience to unintended strategic responses under dynamic market conditions.

title: Multi-LLM Semantic Fusion for Context-Aware Traffic Accident Risk Prediction and Personalized Driver Warnings
authors: AHMET ALBAYRAK; Süleyman ÇEVEN; Raif BAYIR
abstract: Traffic accident prevention requires not only accurate risk prediction but also the ability to communicate context-specific warnings to drivers in an understandable and timely manner. This study proposes a hybrid artificial intelligence framework that integrates machine learning–based accident severity modeling, real-time contextual data processing, and large language model (LLM)–driven semantic warning generation for intelligent driver assistance. The proposed framework combines historical accident records, spatial location data, driver-related variables, meteorological conditions, and real-time GPS information to identify high-risk road segments and generate personalized driver warnings.The study consists of three main stages. First, a survey of 576 drivers was conducted to examine risk perception, route familiarity, perceived adequacy of existing traffic safety measures, and acceptance of intelligent warning systems. The findings revealed strong driver demand for dynamic and context-aware warnings, particularly under heavy traffic conditions, unfamiliar routes, and accident-prone locations. Second, accident severity was modeled using machine learning algorithms, with the Random Forest model achieving the strongest classification performance, including a macro-averaged F1 score of 91.72%. Third, the predicted accident risk indicators were integrated with a multi-LLM semantic interpretation layer to transform numerical risk scores and contextual variables into concise, action-oriented, and personalized warning messages.The proposed mobile-based architecture delivers warnings through visual, auditory, and optional haptic interfaces when drivers approach high-risk locations. By combining predictive risk modeling with natural-language explanation and real-time contextual awareness, the framework moves beyond conventional static warning systems and offers a human-centered decision-support approach for intelligent transportation safety. The results suggest that LLM-augmented semantic fusion can improve the interpretability, personalization, and practical usability of traffic accident risk warning systems.

title: Optimizing National Security Strategies through LLM-Driven Artificial Intelligence Integration
abstract: <p>This paper delves into the rapidly evolving landscape of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) as they pertain to national security, with a particular emphasis on their integration into military applications. Through an in-depth analysis of the United States' progress in assimilating AI technologies into the battle space, the paper seeks to reinvigorate enthusiasm about the potential of AI in safeguarding national interests. Key aspects of this paper include the necessity of protecting AI systems from adversaries, as well as the inherent challenges and risks that come with integrating them into military operations. The paper concludes by underscoring the strategic significance of AI in the realm of national security and outlines a set of strategic imperatives for military leaders and policymakers to ensure success in this critical domain.</p>

title: Optimizing National Security Strategies through LLM-Driven Artificial Intelligence Integration
abstract: As artificial intelligence and machine learning continue to advance, we must understand their strategic importance in national security. This paper focuses on unique AI applications in the military, emphasizes strategic imperatives for success, and aims to rekindle excitement about AI's role in national security. We will examine the United States progress in integrating AI into the battle space, discuss the importance of securing these technologies from adversaries, and explore the challenges and risks associated with their integration. Finally, we will highlight the strategic significance of AI to national security and a set of strategic imperatives for military leaders and policymakers.

title: LLM Security and Guardrail Defense Techniques in Web Applications
abstract: Adversarial attacks pose an important threat to the security and trustworthiness of large language models (LLMs). These models are vulnerable to carefully engineered input designed to exploit their weaknesses, degrade system performance, and extract private information. Practical countermeasures need a strong offensive strategy that includes adversarial scenarios simulation to test how models hold up in various conditions. Adversarial data poisoning and evasion techniques are particularly useful as they can reveal strengths during training and inference processes, respectively. Through systematic identification and mitigation of every vulnerability, organizations can strengthen the model's robustness to real-world attacks. This technical framework also emphasizes the need to embed adversarial simulations into the security cycle of LLMs to prevent risks associated with malicious actors. Via iterative analysis, an organization can increase the robustness of a model and build a resilient infrastructure for secure implementation of LLMs in sensitive/high-level environments.

title: Security and Privacy Testing Automation for LLM-Enhanced Applications in Mobile Devices
venue: International journal of networks and security
abstract: The integration of large language models (LLMs) into mobile applications introduces new vectors for security and privacy vulnerabilities. This study proposes an automated framework for systematically testing LLM-enabled mobile apps, focusing on identifying potential threats such as prompt injection, data leakage, unauthorized access, and adversarial manipulation. The approach combines dynamic analysis, static code inspection, and machine learning-based anomaly detection to evaluate app behaviors in real-time. Our method ensures scalability and efficiency across diverse mobile platforms and LLM configurations. Results demonstrate significant improvements in detection rates and response times compared to conventional manual testing. This work aims to bridge the gap between AI innovation and secure mobile deployment, promoting trust in AI-integrated ecosystems.
